producedBy: An ad-hoc filter of homesteading-leads.json against the markets table, keeping listings we had no row for. The code that produced it was not kept, so this file cannot be regenerated — which is the reason it is committed and the 2.5MB full scrape is not.
note: NOT A USABLE WORKLIST AS IT STANDS. Four of these were read against their own source pages on 2026-09-17 and all four were wrong, in two separate ways: our parseListings borrows a later listing's address when a card has none (index 2, index 23), and homesteading.com's own listings are sometimes internally inconsistent (index 1). Two pairs are exact duplicates, so this is 35 leads and not 37. Nothing here may be written to markets without reading the market's own site first; the directory's name, address and website can each be right while describing three different markets.

leads.name: Arlington Farmers Market
leads.notes: THEIR data, not our parse. homesteading.com's own detail page reads "500 Duncan Rd., Wilmington, DE, 19809", so the scrape was faithful — but the name and the website (stillyvalleychamber.com, the Stillaguamish Valley Chamber in Arlington, WASHINGTON) belong to a different market. Their listing is internally inconsistent; nothing on our side can repair it. Needs the real Arlington WA market looked up from scratch.

leads.name: Vancouver Farmers Market
leads.notes: OUR parse. homesteading.com's detail page reads "605 Esther Street, Vancouver, WA, USA" — we recorded Wilmington, DE. The website came through correct because its regex window in parseListings is 400 chars while field() searches block.slice(0, 8000), so the address reached forward into a later listing's card and borrowed it. Suspect every lead whose address does not match its own name or website.

leads.notes: State recorded as VI (US Virgin Islands); ZIP 05753 and the town Middlebury are Vermont. VT not yet confirmed from a primary source.

leads.name: The Marketplace in Woodrige
leads.notes: OUR parse, and diagnosed exactly. addressText is "3001 Bladensburg Road, NE, Washington, DC"; splitAddress takes the comma-delimited Shape 2 branch, finds "NE" at index 1, and US_STATES accepts it — so a DC QUADRANT SUFFIX became Nebraska, and city became the street. postalCode 20036 came from the loose-zip fallback and is not Bladensburg Road's (20018) either. Reproducible from the string alone; affects every DC address in the scrape.
